# Health CEU Samplers (Licensed Professionals)

_4 offer(s). Part of The Actually-Free Job Training Directory; go [back to the index](../index.md)._

Free continuing-education units for nurses, therapists, and other licensed health workers. These are samplers: real CE credit on specific courses, with rotating catalogs. Always confirm with your licensing board that a course counts for your renewal. Education only; nothing here is medical advice.

| Offer | Provider | What free means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [TRAIN Learning Network](#entry-train-network) | Public Health Foundation | Free account, free courses |
| [CDC TRAIN](#entry-cdc-train) | Centers for Disease Control and Prevention | Free account, free courses |
| [Alzheimer's Association eLearning](#entry-alz-training) | Alzheimer's Association | Free course content; some courses in the library include CE certificates at no cost |
| [Medscape CE](#entry-medscape-ce) | WebMD/Medscape | Free for clinicians with a free account: most CE activities across CME for physicians and CE for nurses are sponsored, so you pay nothing |

<a id="entry-train-network"></a>

### TRAIN Learning Network

**Provider:** Public Health Foundation  
**Link:** <https://www.train.org>

**What it is:** Thousands of public-health courses from CDC, states, universities, and nonprofits, organized in one searchable catalog with completion transcripts.

**What "free" means:** Free account, free courses. Many courses carry CE credit (nursing CNE, CHES, and more) at no charge; the accreditation line is on each course page.

**Paper trail:** Free certificates of completion; legitimate CE certificates where the course's accreditation line says so.

**Time needed:** 30 minutes to several hours per course

**Honest catch:** Catalog quality varies by source. Confirm the course lists your specific credit type (e.g., CNE) before counting it toward renewal.

**Tags:** ceu, health, sign-up, certificate

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-cdc-train"></a>

### CDC TRAIN

**Provider:** Centers for Disease Control and Prevention  
**Link:** <https://www.train.org/cdctrain>

**What it is:** CDC's own branch of the TRAIN network: CDC publications, outbreak-response courses, vaccine science, disease-prevention, and self-care-style public-health content.

**What "free" means:** Free account, free courses. CDC is an accredited continuing-education provider, so most courses that offer credit list CNE (nursing), and others list credit for specific professions.

**Paper trail:** Free CE certificates for completed activities where the accreditation is stated.

**Time needed:** 30 minutes to 6 hours per activity

**Honest catch:** Not every course is CE-bearing. Look at the 'CE offered' list on each activity page before counting hours.

**Tags:** ceu, health, government, sign-up, certificate

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-alz-training"></a>

### Alzheimer's Association eLearning

**Provider:** Alzheimer's Association  
**Link:** <https://training.alz.org>

**What it is:** The Alzheimer's Association's curated e-learning library on dementia care: recognizing change, communication approaches, and care-partner support.

**What "free" means:** Free course content; some courses in the library include CE certificates at no cost. Look for the CE flag per course; the rest you take for free without credit.

**Paper trail:** CE certificates on courses that advertise credit (typically for nurses and care providers).

**Time needed:** 30 minutes to 4 hours per course

**Honest catch:** CE-bearing courses are a moving subset (the catalog changes). Check the course page for the credit-type line before you count the hours.

**Tags:** ceu, health, certificates, sign-up

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-medscape-ce"></a>

### Medscape CE

**Provider:** WebMD/Medscape  
**Link:** <https://www.medscape.org>

**What it is:** Clinician-targeted CE articles, case activities, and panels across nearly every specialty. Browsers block access when they see them coming, but the site functions well in a normal browser window.

**What "free" means:** Free for clinicians with a free account: most CE activities across CME for physicians and CE for nurses are sponsored, so you pay nothing.

**Paper trail:** Free CE certificates; your transcript builds over time inside your Medscape account.

**Time needed:** 15 minutes to 2 hours per activity

**Honest catch:** Activity catalogs rotate as sponsorships rotate. Some CNE sponsors do not license your state's credit types. Bots and script checks can 429-block the site.

**Tags:** ceu, health, sign-up, certificate

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08
